name: misinfo-general
description: This article introduces misinfo-general, a benchmark dataset for evaluating misinformation models' ability to perform out-of-distribution generalization. Misinformation changes rapidly, much more quickly than moderators can annotate at scale, resulting in a shift between the training and inference data distributions. As a result, misinformation detectors need to be able to perform out-of-distribution generalization, an attribute they currently lack. Our benchmark uses distant labelling to enable simulating covariate shifts in misinformation content. We identify time, event, topic, publisher, political bias, misinformation type as important axes for generalization, and we evaluate a common class of baseline models on each. Using article metadata, we show how this model fails desiderata, which is not necessarily obvious from classification metrics. reputation: A recent research benchmark from the misinformation detection literature; it is not yet widely established as a standard community benchmark.
notes: Designed to probe covariate shift and shortcut reliance across time, event, topic, publisher, political bias, and misinformation type; likely sensitive to dataset shift and distant-label noise.
